classification.difficultyReason: Each part is a two-stage evaluation: find the exact inverse-trig angle in its principal range, then apply a second trig function to it. The hardest part, c, needs cos⁻¹ of a negative value, which gives 3π/4 in quadrant II, followed by sine. All the required values are standard and no sign or range reasoning goes beyond that. This is a routine linked procedure, harder than a single direct fact. It is easier than p13-q4, whose parts add a double-angle composition and a surd-simplification step, and easier than p17-q3, which needs domain, range and graph reasoning.
